chat.author: Philippe Dellaert
chat.text: @krooj, do you mean an ACME style solution that hosts CIMD for local agents? I think that's certainly an interesting offering, but does put a dependency on a centralized service. I can see it helpful for many use cases, but I can imagine certain organizations or users might not want to depend on that

chat.author: Karl McGuinness
chat.text: not sure if you are aware, I did publish a profile for actor claim https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-mcguinness-oauth-actor-profile/ to help address this but little feedback on whether this useful

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: There is some debate about whether agent identity is even best conveyed by OAuth or something else (e.g. WIMSE)

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: I see this as a way to include extra information in the OAuth token so that the RS can make better decsions when it reasons over granting access.

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Specifically knowing the agent identty (regardless of how that is expressed or the identifier scehem)

chat.author: Jessica Trochet
chat.text: re: sub/act; one semantic that they provide relative to an agent claim is more clarity around the relative roles that different entities play. an agent claim alone does not necessarily describe the relationship between the agent and some other entity.

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Agreed there is an implioied relationship

chat.author: Jessica Trochet
chat.text: (in other words: agent is closer to a data type than a specific claim field)

chat.author: krooj
chat.text: @philippe Exactly - it's not ideal, but it does close the loop on CIMD requiring a TLS endpoint for the metadata

chat.author: Michael Jones
chat.text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-skyfire-oauth-kyapay-token/ has claims both for the Agent Platform and the Agent Instance

chat.author: Philippe Dellaert
chat.text:
@krooj, I think it brings a potential trust issue into CIMD. At least today with CIMD, there's some correlation between the client, the domain hosting CIMD and ownership of that domain/hosting and the TLS certificate chain. 
For hosting CIMD on a 3rd party, you loose some of that information and depend on verification process by the hosting service for some trust. http-01 & dns-01 do not work there, of course. So it relies possibly on email-reply. 
The trust issue exists with DCR as well, of course! But this possibly introduces it to CIMD. For DCR, AB-DCR could help with that trust management.
Will admit I need to think more about this and this is just my first thoughts. I think it would be a helpful service if someone would implement it. I'm the first to cheer for more options and choices for users to choose from base on their use case.

chat.author: krooj
chat.text: @Philippe - agree on the trust issue, but it does solve for simple localhost cases and DCR cardinality. Something to dig into tho :)

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: @Philippe do take a look at the blog post Paul mentioned on the MCP blog. Also I have a recent post on my blog that gets into this. The tldr is CIMD doesn't have all the answers for clients, but improves the situation enormously compared to all previous options.

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: I think the device (PC, mobile, etc) is less important than the context the agent has - its instructions, guardrails, skills, etc.

chat.author: Jonathan Rosenberg
chat.text: In terms of the end user making a decision to approve it or not

chat.author: Philippe Dellaert
chat.text: @Aaron, I definitely agree that CIMD improves the situation enormously. (I've read your blog, and agree with it). I'm looking at some use cases for which it might not fit.

chat.author: Paul Carleton
chat.text: ^ re: cimd, better supporting local clients seems bound to OS-level support (e.g. binary attestation, similar to anti-cheat). does that line up with the use cases you're considering?

chat.author: Philippe Dellaert
chat.text:
I did not think about those use cases. Couldn't those not use CIMD (if the dev of those clients can host it)? If not, this could be one of the use cases. 
I'm thinking about localhost agents based on open source harnesses (or forks of) which are not in a position to present controlled/centralized CIMD (they don't want to claim the identity for everyone using their FOSS harness/agent)

chat.author: Philippe Dellaert
chat.text: Interesting discussion though. I need to drop for a call, happy to discuss further!

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: @paul is there any involvment of OS providers with platform support? Seems Like MacOS, iOS, and Android sounds ok with platform attestation but what about Microsoft?

chat.author: Efe Kahraman
chat.text: The paper I've been working recently seems to be quite a bit of overlap with the scope broadness problem desribed here I think. I'm happy to share the paper on the mailing list afterwards.

chat.author: krooj
chat.text: @Efe I'd love to see it

chat.author: Paul Carleton
chat.text: @jeff tbh i haven't gotten that far, just that we'd need something there. iirc iOS and Android have something that could in theory be used here, but MacOS and Windows do not.

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: a little birdie told me the iOS API is coming to MacOS in I think the next version

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: oauth absolutely allows that model already, see www-authenticate

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: And the work that was proposed on RS remediated response using RAR is making standardized

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: WWW-Authenticate is an empty vehicule that need more steering

chat.author: Jessica Trochet
chat.text: personally, i think the idea of the discrete authorization service is most productive in the context of an enterprise that operates that service across all the resource services it owns; that authz service is permitted access to sufficiently-rich context about the user intent, which might not be aligned with the idea of the agent as a pure user-agent in the consumer world.

chat.author: George Fletcher
chat.text: Has any consideration be given to the case where the resource is itself an LLM and is working with another disparate set of resource servers? How are the "user desires" managed in this case or is the user actually removed from the downstream decisions?

chat.author: Maxwell Gerber
chat.text:
in the context of an enterprise that operates that service across all the resource services it owns;

DTR helps to enable this by giving the AS a mechanism to defer issuing the token while the AS confers with some other, undefined service. So FooCorp could run a policy engine and ask each AS in each SaaS product to invoke it during grant processing.

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: There are some pretty deep privacy concerns with simply copying the entire context down to the leaf nodes for them to reason on, and so a future where the RS's can figure this out at runtime is pretty essential if you ask me.

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: as in, asking authorities and downscoping from the request context

chat.author: Maxwell Gerber
chat.text:
Karl's https://openid.github.io/authzen/authzen-access-request-approval-profile-1_0.html
being one of the mechanisms where the AS defers decision making to another service

chat.author: Karl McGuinness
chat.text: AuthZen Access Request and Approval enables more of these resource driven, fine grained authorizations that doesn't require persisting permissions

chat.author: Karl McGuinness
chat.text: and composes with work around RAR, DTR, MCP SEPs

chat.author: Karl McGuinness
chat.text: There is oauth binding as well https://github.com/openid/authzen/blob/main/profiles/authzen-access-request-oauth/authzen-access-request-oauth-profile-1_0.md

chat.author: Paul Carleton
chat.text: (brb)

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Authroization is distributed throughout enterprise infrastructure, OAuth is one part of it, but there are several ther systems involved as well.

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: And they all need to signal their peers if they see a request not valid for the other to adjust

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: Yes, authroization also changes over time (or perhaps even mid-transaction - e.g. fraud assesment)

chat.author: Omri Gazitt
chat.text: Ideally they are operating over a common policy - at the granularity of scopes at the AS, and individual resources at the RS

chat.author: Paul Carleton
chat.text: Yep, agreed. it's not necessarily all on OAuth to solve, and we shouldn't try to cram everything into the access token (privacy considerations as Justin mentioned!)

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: In practice, I think we need to do more on metadata discovery for authroization sytems to make it easier to combine systems.

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
chat.text: But it is a composition problem

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: for the tiered payments questions I would recommend the community look into what OpenPayment has been doing with RAR-type objects: https://openpayments.dev/

chat.author: Pieter Kasselman
